steps.body: Flat shapes have names! A **circle** is perfectly round. A **triangle** has 3 straight sides. A **square** has 4 equal sides.

widget.prompt: Which shape is perfectly round, like a coin?

hotspots.label: square
hotspots.feedback: A square has 4 straight sides and corners — the round one is the circle.

hotspots.label: triangle
hotspots.feedback: A triangle has 3 pointy corners — the round one is the circle.

hotspots.label: rectangle
hotspots.feedback: A rectangle has corners — round with no corners is the circle.

widget.missFeedback: Look at the sides and corners of each shape, then tap the one the question describes.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — a circle is round all the way, like a coin or a clock.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents name shapes.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for name shapes must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines name shapes.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

steps.body: A **rectangle** is like a door: 4 sides, but two are long and two are short.

explanationVariants: Three straight sides and three corners — that shape is a triangle.
A slice of pizza has a triangle shape: 3 sides.

widget.prompt: A shape has 3 straight sides, like a slice of pizza. What is it?

hotspots.label: circle
hotspots.feedback: A circle has NO straight sides — three sides makes a triangle.

hotspots.label: square
hotspots.feedback: A square has 4 sides — THREE sides makes a triangle.

hotspots.label: hexagon
hotspots.feedback: A hexagon has 6 sides — three makes a triangle.

widget.missFeedback: Look at the sides and corners of each shape, then tap the one the question describes.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — TRI means three: 3 sides, 3 corners.

widget.prompt: A door shape has 4 sides — two long, two short. What is it?

hotspots.label: circle
hotspots.feedback: A circle has no sides at all — the door shape is a rectangle.

hotspots.label: triangle
hotspots.feedback: A triangle has only 3 sides — the door shape is a rectangle.

hotspots.label: square
hotspots.feedback: A square's sides are all the SAME — a door's long-and-short shape is a rectangle.

widget.missFeedback: Look at the sides and corners of each shape, then tap the one the question describes.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — a rectangle is the door shape: long and short sides.

explanationVariants: All 4 sides the same length makes it a square.
A cracker with equal sides is a square.

widget.prompt: A cracker has 4 sides that are ALL the same length. What shape is it?

hotspots.label: circle
hotspots.feedback: A circle has no sides — four equal sides is a square.

hotspots.label: rectangle
hotspots.feedback: A rectangle has long AND short sides — all-equal is a square.

hotspots.label: triangle
hotspots.feedback: A triangle has 3 sides — this has 4 equal ones: square.

widget.successFeedback: Yes — four equal sides makes a square.

pairErrors.feedback: A door has corners — round-with-no-corners is the coin's circle.

widget.missFeedback: Look at each thing: round, pointy with 3 sides, or door-like?
widget.successFeedback: All matched — coin, slice, door: circle, triangle, rectangle!

explanationVariants: A hexagon has 6 sides — like a honeycomb cell.

widget.prompt: A honeycomb shape is turned on its side. It still has 6 straight sides. What is it still called?

options.label: A triangle
options.feedback: A triangle has 3 sides. Turning never changes 6 sides into 3.

options.label: A hexagon
options.feedback: Yes — 6 sides makes a hexagon, even when it is turned.

options.label: A circle
options.feedback: A circle has no straight sides. This shape still has 6.

options.label: A square
options.feedback: A square has 4 sides. This one still has 6, so it is a hexagon.
